partialCapture.note: Neither the 456-frame sweep nor the 12-theme sweep was regenerated. Frames added or refreshed here were captured against the same guards (assertFramePaints) but only in the two brand themes, and the live-app frames came from the real Electron window rather than Storybook. The spacing round REFRESHED the five chat-tool-rows surfaces because the row pitch changed under them, and added two: `spacing-uniformity` reproduces the three runs the operator screenshotted, `turn-boundary` shows the hierarchy that survives the tightening. `narrow` and `working-labels` are now captured in a viewport sized to their content — at 1280x900 they were mostly empty ground and crossed the uniformity ceiling once the rows tightened. REMEDIATION ROUND 1: all seven chat-tool-rows surfaces were refreshed again, because the name/summary gutter, the running row's live clock, the sr-only outcome text and the summary fallback all changed what they show. REMEDIATION ROUND 2: `real-conversation-tool-rows` was RE-CAPTURED and is no longer stale. It now shows 38 real tool rows with 0 blank object columns on a 20px pitch, rendered by the shipped reducer and the shipped CanonicalTranscript over real /history pages paged oldest-first in 20-entry pages (the cross-page condition the blank-summary defect needed). Electron is not required for this surface — the desktop API answers a plain bearer request. The reading was proven falsifiable by running the SAME harness with the reducer starved: stripping tool_calls alone still yields 0 blanks (the output fallback carries it), stripping tool_calls AND output yields 53 of 53 blank, reproducing the original defect from the current head.
partialCapture.refreshedNote: REFRESHED: the eight `chat-tool-rows--*` surfaces, in the two brand themes, after the row's object column and its duration/byte spellings changed (a settling frame with no arguments now recovers the call's arguments, the stand-in line steps over the harness's own `exit code: 0` wiring, a sub-50 ms call reads `<0.1s` and the dictation counter reads `KB`/`MB`). RENAMED: `docs/evidence/tool-rows` -> `docs/evidence/chat-tool-rows`, because the capture names a surface from its story title slug and the title gained a `Chat/` prefix after the set was first written; a refresh now lands in the new name, and leaving both would have split one surface family across two directories. The sweep total is 480 rather than 492 because the add-then-rename sequence counted twelve frames twice (the five surfaces that existed under both names); this note is the correction, and a full sweep re-derives the number anyway. NOT REFRESHED: `real-conversation-tool-rows`, whose capture harness is not in this repo - it is the one committed surface whose durations predate the `<0.1s` spelling. ADDED OUTSIDE THE SWEEP: `chat-tool-rows/joined-mid-turn/before/*.webp`, the same story captured from unmodified `origin/main` through the same harness, kept beside the fixed frames so the before/after pair is one directory. A sweep cannot regenerate them (it would capture the current tree), so they are evidence of record and are counted in the sweep total rather than declared as a set.

supplementary.why: The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.
